title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 101
paragraphs: When he had sailed through the fleet and had disembarked from his ship, he sent for Demaratus son of Ariston, who was marching with him against Greece. When Demaratus was brought, Xerxes asked him this: “Demaratus, it now pleases me to ask you something I wish to know. You are not only a Greek, but also, as I have been told both by you and by the other Greeks who speak with me, of a city that is neither the smallest nor the weakest in Greece. Tell me, therefore, whether the Greeks will bring themselves to raise a hand against me. In my own view, even if all the Greeks and the other peoples of the west were gathered together, they would not be strong enough in battle to withstand my attack, if they should be my enemies. Still, I would like to hear your own opinion, whatever you have to say about these matters.” So he asked, and the other replied: “O king, shall I speak the truth to you, or that which will please?” Xerxes bade him speak the truth, saying that he would suffer nothing unpleasant in consequence, any more than he had before.
